page: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system includes 1360.0 GB of system memory, providing 14.17 GB per core. For acceleration, it features eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs from the Ampere family, delivering a combined 640 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of 3216 GB of NVMe SSD capacity.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, rank in the bottom 25 percent, and single-threaded compression tasks show similar constraints. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25 percent with a stress-ng multi-core score of 75780.48. Memory read bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 4212.24 GB/sec for small cached blocks. Large-block write bandwidth and database operations perform in the average tier.

The server excels in GPU-driven workloads, particularly large language model inference. It achieves top-tier performance in prompt processing across small, medium, and large models, processing 410.88 tokens per second for 70B models. Text generation for medium and large models also ranks in the top 10 percent. This hardware profile is optimized for deep learning, LLM inference, ray tracing, and high-throughput Redis database operations, though it presents a tradeoff of lower single-threaded CPU efficiency.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server designed for demanding parallel computing workloads. It features 96 vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon processors, 1360.0 GB of system memory, and 3216 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server is equipped with eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs, providing a total of 640 GB of VRAM. While single-core CPU benchmarks and single-threaded compression tasks perform in the lower tier, the instance delivers strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory read bandwidth. Benchmark data highlights top-tier capabilities in large language model inference, especially for prompt processing and text generation across medium and large models. This server is highly suited for deep learning, large-scale LLM deployment, ray tracing, and high-throughput database operations like Redis, where massive GPU acceleration and high memory density are required.
